reasoning: Hard gates failed: kelvin_ok=false (SENSEC1 both HI/LO unrouted, SENSEC2_HI unrouted), DRC=25 (zero required). The stub summary is the diagnostic: final stub nets=['/CAN_H','/I2C_SCL','/I2C_SDA'] — zero Kelvin nets survived compilation despite absorbed=5 and trimmed_spurs=2 starting from n_stubs=7. Rule 8 unconditionally requires aborting with stub_compiler_silent_failure when the board netlist contains /SENSEC* pairs and the post-compilation stub list has zero /SENSEC* entries with compile_failures empty. That abort did not fire; FR dispatched anyway and produced the predictable Kelvin failure. Separately, SENSEC2 is an asymmetric case: SENSEC2_HI appears in failing_reasons but SENSEC2_LO does not, triggering Rule 4's coordinate re-derivation requirement. The root problem in every round since the Kelvin rules were written is the same: the stub compiler silently absorbs or trims Kelvin stubs, the enforcement abort doesn't fire, FR routes without them, and the Kelvin gate fails. Adding another variant of the same rule has not changed behaviour. The one genuinely new structural gap is that Rule 4 (re-derive asymmetric cable coordinates) has no carry-forward mechanism: after detecting SENSEC2's asymmetric failure the manager re-derives coordinates once, but if the next round's stub compiler again absorbs the stub there is no persistent check that forces the issue until BOTH HI and LO are confirmed routed. The existing rules only look backwards (prior round) or at round-zero conditions; none maintain a cross-round 'must appear in output' obligation tied to a named net. The scorer penalty side has nothing new to offer: kelvin_unrouted and gate_fail are already at 1000 each, and the real bottleneck is that FR never receives the Kelvin stubs, making scorer weight irrelevant to convergence.
manager_rule: After any round where an asymmetric Kelvin result is detected for cable N (one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO appears in failing_reasons while its partner does not), add that cable's two net names to a persistent 'kelvin_force_recheck' set that survives across round boundaries. At every subsequent FR dispatch, before allowing the stub nets list to be finalised, the manager must verify that BOTH nets of every cable in kelvin_force_recheck appear in the final stub nets list. If either net is absent — regardless of whether compile_failures is empty, absorbed counts seem small, or trimmed_spurs seems harmless — inject an explicit compile_failure for the absent net by name and abort the dispatch per Rule 3. A cable is removed from kelvin_force_recheck only after a round in which BOTH its HI and LO nets are absent from failing_reasons (i.e., both confirmed routed). This cross-round carry-forward is distinct from Rule 4's single-round re-derivation requirement: Rule 4 ensures correct coordinates are re-derived; this rule ensures the re-derived stub actually survives to FR dispatch in every subsequent round until the cable is clean.
